ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-loop circuit. On the right side is a capacitor, labeled 10 μF, with the upper end of the capacitor positive and the lower end negative, and the initial voltage is marked as V(0−)=10 V. At the top of the circuit there is a switch, labeled as closed at t=0. On the left side, a 10 kΩ resistor and an ideal Zener diode are connected in series, and the Zener voltage is labeled as VZ=5 V. Reasoning: After the switch is closed, the capacitor discharges through the 10 kΩ resistor and the ideal Zener diode. As long as the capacitor voltage vC is greater than 5 V, the Zener is in breakdown conduction state, and the voltage across it remains 5 V. Therefore the loop current is i(t)=(vC−5)/R. The capacitor discharge satisfies C dvC/dt=−(vC−5)/R. From the initial value vC(0)=10 V, solving gives vC(t)=5+(10−5)e^(−t/RC), so i(t)=[(10−5)/R]e^(−t/RC). The total energy dissipated in the Zener is EZ=∫0∞ VZ i(t) dt=5∫0∞[(10−5)/R]e^(−t/RC)dt=5C(10−5). Substituting C=10 μF, EZ=5×10×10^−6×5=250×10^−6 J=0.25 mJ. To three decimal places, it is 0.250 mJ.

Solve the exponential decay from 10 V toward 5 V. Compute total Zener energy as EZ=∫0∞ 5·i(t) dt = 5∫0∞[(10-5)/R]e^{-t/(RC)}dt = 5C(10-5), then convert joules to mJ to obtain 0.25 mJ.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit elements and polarities seen in the image. Determine that the capacitor discharges from 10 V down to the Zener clamp level 5 V, not to 0 V. Compute the charge delivered through the series branch as ΔQ = 10 µF × (10 V − 5 V) = 50 µC. Since the ideal Zener has a constant 5 V drop for all this transferred charge, compute EZ = 5 V × 50 µC = 250 µJ = 0.25 mJ.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The circuit shows a 10 µF capacitor on the right with its upper plate marked positive and initial voltage V(0-) = 10 V. A switch at the top is open initially and is closed at t = 0. The left branch contains a 10 kΩ resistor in series with an ideal Zener diode labeled VZ = 5 V. Reasoning: After the switch closes, the initially charged capacitor discharges through the series resistor-Zener path only while the capacitor voltage exceeds the Zener clamp voltage. The capacitor therefore falls from 10 V to 5 V, not to 0 V. The charge delivered through the Zener branch is ΔQ = CΔV = 10 µF × (10 V − 5 V) = 50 µC. For an ideal Zener conducting at constant 5 V, the energy dissipated in it is EZ = VZ ΔQ = 5 V × 50 µC = 250 µJ = 0.25 mJ.
